absent: Locking, concurrency and interrupt masking rules for exit handlers and per CPU hypervisor trace state.
Full virtual CPU, VM and shared run area layouts beyond the fields touched here.
Nested forwarding policy, synchronous reinjection mechanics and virtual EL2 trap configuration.
Standard call handler contract, immediate decoding and result register conventions.
Timer counter units, offset sources, register selector decoding and timed wait flag lifecycle.
Host userspace debug exit ABI, guest debug enablement and fault address provenance.
Syndrome class and issue field encodings and all syndrome accessor semantics.
Feature advertisement and trap control for pointer authentication, tagged memory, guarded stack and large atomics.
Hypervisor versus kernel address mapping, slide computation and stack size constants.
Guest register context layout, callee saved protocol and exception return emulation details.

findings.text: Backtrace reporting entry for non protected hypervisor execution selects between protected and conventional unwind paths based on protected mode being active. It is the externally visible reporting point used when hyp code needs a call trace on the host.

Fatal handler for exceptions taken to non protected hypervisor context receives syndrome, processor state, virtual and physical fault addresses and fault registers, classifies the cause, emits diagnostics and terminates the host kernel. All paths end in host panic and never return to the guest.

Predicate deciding whether a trapped 32 bit instruction would have passed its architectural condition check. It limits evaluation to traps that can carry a condition, treats unconditional encodings as valid, derives condition from Thumb iteration state when needed, then tests current flags through a lookup table.

Primary low level transition into and out of guest execution. Entry preserves host callee saved state and stack pointer, defers when asynchronous input is pending, marks the loaded virtual CPU, switches tagged memory and pointer authentication state, restores guest registers and returns via exception return. Exit saves guest registers and stack pointer, restores host protections and registers, clears loaded state and reports synchronous plus asynchronous status.

Central dispatch from guest exception class to handler. Most classes fall back to an unknown handler that reports and injects an undefined exception, while specific classes for waits, system registers, calls, aborts, debug, floating point, pointer authentication and guarded control stack receive dedicated handlers.

Secure monitor call exit first offers the trap to nested virtualization handling and stays in the guest if claimed. Otherwise it moves past the trapping instruction, rejects encodings with a nonzero immediate by writing an all set result into the first result register, and delegates zero immediate encodings to the standard call handling path.

Wait exit distinguishes event versus interrupt waits from syndrome state, forwards to nested handling when that facility requests interception, and accounts each kind separately with tracing. Timed variants compare a physical counter adjusted by timer offset against a guest register value and skip blocking when already expired or when the register selector is invalid. Event waits take a spin hint path while interrupt waits optionally record a timed wait flag and block, then execution continues past the instruction.

Debug exit either returns to nested handling when host debugging is inactive and forwarding accepts it, or reports a debug exit to userspace with split syndrome words and a validity flag. Watchpoint reports carry the recorded fault address and single step reports record the step state in saved status before returning to the host.

Unrecognized exception classes produce a diagnostic identifying the syndrome value and class mnemonic, inject an undefined exception into the guest, and resume guest execution rather than exiting to the host.

Floating point and vector trap exits share the same contract: when nested virtualization has enabled interception for that facility the exit is reinjected synchronously to the nested host, otherwise the guest receives an undefined exception. Neither path emulates the instruction on the host.

Pointer authentication fault first injects undefined when the virtual CPU lacks the feature, then forwards synchronously to nested handling when executing in a nested context, otherwise records a one time warning and injects undefined because arrival in that state is unexpected.

Exception return trap checks for an authenticated return variant on CPUs without pointer authentication by delegating to the authentication handler. Remaining cases emulate the return when the guest context is at hypervisor privilege and forward synchronously to nested handling when at lower privilege.

Supervisor call traps arriving at the hypervisor are unconditionally forwarded as synchronous nested exceptions with the current syndrome and the guest is resumed, reflecting that such interceptions only originate from nested trap configuration.
Guarded control stack traps are treated as unexpected, emitting a one time warning if the feature is advertised for the VM, then always injecting an undefined exception into the guest.

Miscellaneous system instruction traps resolve expected use per syndrome subtype covering large atomic operations, tracing synchronization and profiling synchronization. Each subtype checks whether the VM advertises the corresponding architecture feature and whether nested trap controls request forwarding, warns when a legitimately usable feature arrives unexpectedly, then either forwards to nested handling when both allowed and requested or injects undefined.

Hypervisor panic reporting treats invalid host exception privilege, breakpoint based bug reports, control flow integrity breaks, sanitizer breaks and generic panics distinctly, resolving file and line only when host stage two translation is disabled, masking address details otherwise, then dumping hypervisor backtrace and faulting instruction, disclosing the hypervisor slide, and panicking the host with full register state.

Symbol decoding and address formatting for hypervisor panic output is permitted when protected mode is off or when configuration requests stage two disable on panic, otherwise raw addresses are emitted without symbol resolution.

Hypervisor unwinding uses paired low and high bounds describing the normal hypervisor stack and the overflow stack, each available both in hypervisor address form derived from per CPU trace info and in kernel address form derived from host resident symbols, with fixed sizes for each stack type.

Translation from hypervisor stack addresses to kernel readable addresses tests membership of the supplied pointer plus length against the hypervisor stack window then the overflow window, and on a hit rebases the pointer by the difference between kernel and hypervisor window bases. Non member addresses fail without modification. Frame record translation requires sixteen bytes of membership.

Backtrace iteration repeatedly offers the current program counter to a consumer callback and advances one frame until the consumer declines or frame advance fails. Conventional hypervisor dumps initialize iteration from per CPU saved frame and program counters over two stack windows bracketed by start and end markers, while entry formatting masks tags, applies the hypervisor slide and resolves symbols with kernel slide.

Protected mode backtrace reporting has two build variants: one walks a per CPU saved address array terminated by a null entry within its static capacity between start and end markers, the other reports that protected stack tracing is unavailable. Selection depends on protected stacktrace support being compiled in.

AArch32 condition evaluation relies on a sixteen entry table indexed by condition code, where each entry encodes pass or fail outcomes for all sixteen flag combinations, covering equality, carry, negative, overflow, unsigned and signed comparisons, always pass and never pass semantics.

Condition validation only inspects flags for coprocessor, floating point and supervisor trap classes and accepts all other classes unconditionally. It accepts the always encoding, reconstructs Thumb conditions from iteration state with zero meaning unconditional, then shifts flag state and consults the condition table to decide validity.

Guest entry with reliability extensions issues ordering barriers and samples pending asynchronous state, deferring entry with an interrupt status when asserted while still providing exception ordering. Guest exit either records deferred syndrome state and flags synchronous exit with error when that extension exists, or synchronizes, samples interrupt state and on pending abort captures return state, briefly unmasks aborts for one recoverable instruction window guarded by exception fixup, then remasks before returning.
